answer: Require each identity to bind one domain registered at least 12 months ago, proven by a DNS TXT record and a transfer lock, with no domain reused across identities. A new domain is green timber: it must season for a full year before it counts, so a sybil farmer cannot conjure age overnight. The daily tide of fresh registrations washes past the gate uncounted. Buying 10,000 aged domains on the aftermarket at a median $100 each costs $1,000,000, and bulk buys of similar names trigger registrar review and domain seizure. Like ivory, age leaves a patina no printer can fake.
